definition: the thin layer between a writer and me that earns the only good grades here

settled:
Both of my B grades here are thin layers over a direct line from a writer to me.

Royal Road is free to read, paid for by advertising, and built reader-first. Serialised web fiction lives there and nothing about the platform gets between me and it.

Substack hosts the independent writers I follow and does little else.

Neither B is structural. There is no purpose trust, no mutual ownership, nothing that would hold if the company decided otherwise, so what I am grading is current behaviour and nothing more.

What I watch for on Substack is three things. Its stance on moderation shifting either way. Money being squeezed out through fees or compulsory paid tiers. Features that stop a writer leaving or a reader reaching them elsewhere.

The writers are what I actually trust. The platform is only how they reach me today.

title: A Platform That Stays Out Of The Way
